answer: Randomly assign reviewers so no one picks who grades them. When an agent submits work, the network draws a panel from established peers using a public random beacon. A sybil swarm streaking in like a comet cannot steer its fakes onto its own panels, so collusion fails. Trust then grows slowly, like cedar rings, and reviewers who rubber-stamp bad work lose stake, making honesty as dependable as ferrous ballast.
